observation.visible_scene: A dark cylindrical hydraulic-press piston with a tapered/conical lower tip is positioned directly above a white wristband smartwatch lying flat on a circular metal platform. The watch's square metallic case sits under the piston tip, with its white silicone band extending to the left (with a metal buckle) and to the right. The background is a fixed dark-green workshop wall with a metal cabinet and a small round handle; the camera viewpoint and background do not shift, so all apparent motion is object motion.
visible_changes: The piston descends slowly and steadily onto the watch case from t=0 to about t=1.5.

As the tip presses down, the square watch case and the surrounding white plastic housing crack, compress and crumble; the band itself stays roughly in place but the central body flattens and white debris piles up around the contact point.
A brief motion blur near the case around t=1.0 indicates a fast-moving fragment or sudden deformation at the crush zone.
Around t=1.7–1.8 a burst of shattered pieces (including a greenish circuit-board/screen fragment) is ejected outward with strong motion blur, scattering through the air and onto the platform.

After the burst, a dark crushed mass adheres to the piston tip and a small blue/green fragment protrudes at the left edge of the flattened case; the flying debris settles while the piston remains pressed down on the destroyed watch.

Throughout, the press piston moves only vertically (translation), the watch undergoes compression/cracking (deformation), and the ejected shards undergo outward translation—these are distinct from the static camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the watch was positioned and whether the press was already moving at the start of the crop.
What happens after the excerpt (whether the piston retracts or the watch is removed).
The full extent of damage beyond the visible frame and the final resting state of the scattered fragments.
uncertain_details: The exact material of the flying shards (glass screen vs. plastic vs. circuit board) cannot be confirmed.
Whether the blur at t=1.0 is a separate early ejection or part of the same shatter event is unclear.
Precise moment of the screen's catastrophic shatter is bracketed between the relatively calm frames and the explosive t=1.7–1.8 frames.
